messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: p95 latency spike detected on shared-gpu-pool-c (12:03:15). Affected tenants: t-ARGO, t-BETA. Throughput down ~35%. Auto-remediation not triggered (threshold margin hit).

ashley: seeing this too. p95 jumped from ~60ms -> 420ms across several hosts in pool-c. Any obvious noisy tenant?

michael: quick skim of runtime logs shows repeated kernel fallback on host gpu-13 to 'matmul_generic' and 'attention_fallback' around 12:03:14. suspecting kernel selection thrash. snippet: ```
[12:03:14.112] kernel_select: model=redwood-7b seq=153 chosen=optimized_fmha fp16
[12:03:14.115] kernel_select: model=redwood-7b seq=316 chosen=matmul_generic fallback_reason=sequence_length_mismatch
[12:03:14.118] runtime_perf: kv_cache_evicted=128 host=gpu-13
```

sasha: kv_cache metrics show spike in evictions and cache churn for t-ARGO around same time. eviction_rate jumped to 0.43. graph: `kv_cache/evictions{tenant=t-ARGO}`.

raj: scheduler logs show batcher toggled to small-batch mode due to headroom checks failing on several workers. Config excerpt: ```
batcher: 
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  min_batch_delay_ms: 2
  qos_threshold: 0.85
```
At ~12:03, worker free_mem dipped under soft_limit triggering immediate flush -> smaller batches -> bad perf.

ashley: does this look like a noisy-tenant memory pressure -> kernel fallback -> batching collapse cascade?

michael: yeah. Additional detail: a quantization tuning (QAT) training job from t-BETA was observed holding CUDA pinned pages on same host for a short window. That reduced available GPU allocation for inference kernels and caused our kernel selector (which prefers tiled kernels) to pick generic kernels for borderline shapes.

ops-sre: I'm going to put a soft throttle on t-ARGO and bump its per-tenant GPU memory quota on pool-c to stop re-triggering. Will also isolate the QAT job if it's still running. Doing now.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Applied tenant throttle=0.6 for tenant=t-ARGO on pool=shared-gpu-pool-c to hosts [gpu-11,gpu-12,gpu-13]. Action id: dpl-7721.

ashley: after throttling p95 dropped back to ~85ms within 90s. throughput returned. Thanks.

sasha: we should still follow up: proposed remediation list in INF-3587 (created):
- add guardrail in kernel selector to avoid thrashing between optimized and generic kernels within a short window (cooldown)
- per-tenant KV-cache soft quotas and early backpressure signals rather than full eviction cascade
- improve batcher sampling so single-host memory pressure doesn't force global small-batch mode (make batch decisions per-host)
- run a simulated repro harness with a QAT-like memory holder to validate fixes

michael: +1. I sketched a patch to kernel selector with a 10s cooldown and a telemetry counter `kernel_fallback_rapid` that will trigger alerting. Will open PR after quick unit tests.

raj: also recommend a short-term mitigation: prefer fallback to a compatible quantized kernel instead of matmul_generic when memory shapes mismatch and quantized variant exists. probably lower perf but fewer lat spikes.

ops-sre: filed a short incident blurb to #incidents. tagging infra and runtime owners.

ashley: thanks all. action items assigned: michael (kernel cooldown PR), sasha (kv quotas design), raj (quantized-fallback proposal), ops-sre (tenant isolation+) — we'll sync tomorrow 10:30. :thumbsup:
